findings.title: In panel review mode, a single-entry review chain hits needs_human whenever a finding is raised
findings.detail: With a review chain, the verifier call goes through `call(request, constraints, ...)` with verifierConstraints(), which still sets `excludeModels: avoidModels` (the finders' models, reason "raised a candidate it would verify"). In chain mode this hard exclusion is kept; only `verify`-role excludeModels are cleared in context.ts:480. If cfg.reviewMode is "panel" and the operator pins one review model, every finder routes to that model. The verifier then excludes it, the chain is empty, and the run stops at needs_human. findings.title: Legacy eligibility uses a hardcoded commit timestamp, not the install's upgrade time
findings.detail: A run is marked worktree_provenance='legacy' only if its prepare stage started before 1791099304000 (2026-10-04 07:35:04 UTC, when 7405d9f was committed), with no later prepare. An install doesn't switch to #323 when it is committed; it switches when it upgrades. The request says the fix matters for 'the next install that upgrades with runs in flight'. On such an install, every run prepared on the old release after that instant is not marked legacy. hasLegacyWorktree returns false, so no record is written, and the next headSha/git call fails with 'Missing trusted Git paths', which is exactly the original incident. Even on this machine, runs prepared between the commit and the actual restart
findings.failure_scenario: An install running the pre-#323 release prepares a run on 2026-11-01, parks it, then upgrades to this release. The migration leaves worktree_provenance NULL, resume skips recording, and `await headSha(worktree)` throws 'Missing trusted Git paths'. The run fails.

findings.title: Far over the ≤20-line budget; parallel reimplementation of worktree trust logic
findings.detail: The request asks for a single recordWorktree call on resume, or a migration step, within 20 source lines. The change adds a 71-line module that independently rediscovers the admin dir: it scans worktrees/*, runs `worktree list` against the cache, checks uid/nlink/recursive inspection and pointer comparisons. It also adds a DB column, a time-based SQL heuristic and two store methods. This duplicates and diverges from trustedEnv/recordWorktree in src/git/command.ts. For example, it rejects config files that trustedEnv allows in the admin dir, and it adds a uid check. Future changes now have two sources of truth to keep in sync.
findings.failure_scenario: Later hardening of trustedEnv is not mirrored in legacy.ts, so legacy recording accepts or rejects worktrees differently from the main check.

findings.title: Every resume now runs a git call before the needsHumanReason check
findings.detail: `await headSha(worktree)` runs unconditionally whenever the worktree exists, before `if (ctx.state.needsHumanReason) throw new NeedsHumanError(...)`. A parked needs_human run whose worktree Git state is broken or unrecorded now fails with a generic git error instead of returning to needs_human. That loses the human-facing reason. It also adds a git subprocess on every resume, even though this check isn't needed to record the worktree.

findings.title: Feed excerpt is the start of the job log, not the failure
findings.detail: `emit` is called with `log || f.line`, and the excerpt is `excerpt.trim().slice(0, 2000)`. For GitHub Actions jobs, the first 2000 characters of the raw log are runner setup output (runner version, image details, checkout). findings.title: A rerun that ends with a conclusion other than success or a failure stays pending forever
findings.detail: In the loop that resolves pending reruns, a completed job whose conclusion is neither `success` nor in `bad` hits `else continue`. Examples are `neutral` or `skipped`, or a failure while main is red on that check. The row stays `rerunning`. When the rollup is SUCCESS, `classifyCi` keeps returning false because a pending rerun exists, so `record()` returns null on every poll. That means repeated REST inspection and `complete = false` for the repository.

findings.title: PATCH cannot clear a runtime model's default effort
findings.detail: `patch` merges the old definition with the patch and revalidates with modelSchema. `effort: undefined` is dropped by JSON and `effort: null` is rejected by `z.enum(...).optional()`. So once a runtime model has a default effort, PATCH can't remove it. That matters because the GUIDE tells operators to omit the default effort for Claude-backed local agent roles. Narrowing `efforts` to exclude the old default also fails with 'absent from efforts' unless a new default is supplied.

findings.detail: `main()` constructs `new Store(cfg.paths.db)` to read runtime models and enable overrides. The Store constructor runs migrations, so a deploy smoke run applies migrations, or creates the DB, from a process other than the daemon. That could happen before the new daemon starts. The migrations are additive, so this is likely harmless, but it is an unexpected side effect for a read-only check.

findings.title: Session-start digest makes sequential per-run detail requests over the whole unacked feed
findings.detail: For every distinct runId in the retained feed after the cursor, digest sequentially calls GET /api/runs/:id (full RunDetail including stages/invocations/artifacts) plus GET /api/land when the run has a PR. The documented hook uses --consumer claude, but agents ack through limitless_feed_ack with whatever consumer they choose, and the digest never acks. So the backlog for 'claude' commonly stays at cursor 0 and the whole retained feed is re-scanned every session.

findings.title: Quoting does not escape bidi override or zero-width characters in untrusted PR text
findings.detail: quote() relies on JSON.stringify plus escaping U+007F–U+009F and U+2028/2029. Bidi controls (U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069) and zero-width characters (U+200B–U+200F, U+FEFF) pass through unescaped into the session context, so a hostile PR title can visually reorder or hide text inside the quotes.

findings.title: Status reports an outdated failed review round when the PR snapshot lacks headRefOid
findings.detail: approvalIsLatest requires approval.sha === pr?.headRefOid. When the saved snapshot has no headRefOid (the field is optional), a newer approval does not hide an older failed or cancelled round, so status reports 'Review changes failed' instead of the approved or head-unknown state.

findings.title: Unrequested change to the publication gate; it blocks text that needs exactly 5 decode rounds, even with an empty denylist
findings.detail: privateMatches is the shared denylist check used by the publication gates (audit.ts, engine checkPrivateText, repos.ts blob scan, github-notifier, land queue). The diff makes it decode repeatedly and adds \uXXXX unescaping. If decoding hasn't settled after 5 rounds, it returns a synthetic entry 0, which blocks publication. The loop also gives up one round early: after the 5th decode it never checks whether a 6th would be stable, so input that settles after exactly 5 decodes is rejected. Entry 0 is returned even when private-strings.txt is empty. The MCP/digest feature didn't need this change to publication gating, and it makes the change bigger than the ~200-line budget.

A registered multiline credential therefore survives in FailureExcerpts even though the combined output is successfully redacted. Exact focused command: bun -e 'import {registerCredential} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; import {redactGateOutput} from "./src/gates/output.ts"; import {FailureExcerpts} from "./src/gates/failures.ts"; const s="synthetic-private-key-line1\nsynthetic-private-key-line2"; registerCredential("PROBE",s); const f=new FailureExcerpts(); for(const line of (`error: ${s}\n(fail) asserti
findings.failure_scenario: A failing check prints a registered two-line credential in assertion diagnostics, followed by (fail) assertion. GateResult.failures retains the complete credential and forwards it into artifacts, land logs and model feedback.

gold.summary: Lossy excerpt line framing prevents matching multiline credentials before storage.
Failure excerpt collection retains unbounded bytes on very long output lines.

findings.title: Privacy filter now withholds any text containing "[redacted]" (unrequested, untested)
findings.detail: `loadOutputPrivacy` used to redact credentials and pass the rest of the text through. Now any string that already contains the literal "[redacted]" is replaced wholesale with "[withheld: private text]". This filter feeds MCP tool outputs and the digest command, not just gate output. Agent tool results are already redacted by the harnesses, and gate output is now redacted at the source, so many run errors, states and titles that used to be partly readable will now be withheld completely. No test exercises the new condition, and the request didn't ask for any change here.
findings.failure_scenario: A run's error field contains "auth failed for token [redacted]" (redacted by a harness or gate). Before: MCP `run_status` returns that text. After: it returns "[withheld: private text]", so the operator loses the diagnostic.

findings.title: Every HTTP JSON response and SSE message is now JSON round-tripped through redactGateData
findings.detail: `json()` and the SSE `send()` now pass every payload through `redactGateData`. That function strips VT control characters from every string, and it adds a `confinementError` field to any object that has `ok` and string `output` properties, whether or not it is a gate result. This is a global change to API output, outside the requested design (redact once in runGates, plus the deploy gate). It also adds a full JSON parse/stringify plus a redaction pass with every credential variant on every response and streamed event.
findings.failure_scenario: Any API payload with an object of shape {ok, output} (e.g. a non-gate status object) gains `confinementError: false/true`, and any ANSI-formatted strings sent to the UI lose their formatting. Every SSE message also pays a JSON parse/stringify plus a redaction pass with every credential variant.

findings.title: Artifact endpoint re-serialises pretty-printed JSON artifacts into compact JSON
findings.detail: `redactGateArtifact` parses every artifact as JSON and returns `JSON.stringify(...)` with no indentation. Artifacts such as `gates-N.json` and `baseline-gates.json` are stored with `JSON.stringify(x, null, 2)` and shown as text in the UI (ui/api.ts:112), so they now display as a single line.
findings.failure_scenario: Opening gates-1.json in the run UI shows one long line instead of the indented document.

findings.title: RunContext rewrites all loaded run state through redactGateData
findings.detail: Every RunContext construction JSON round-trips the whole persisted state. That strips control characters from every string (not just gate output) and adds `confinementError` to any object with ok/output. The next save persists the result. That migrates unrelated data as a side effect, beyond the requested single redaction point.
findings.failure_scenario: A stored state field containing intentional control characters (e.g. feedback text with ANSI) is silently changed and re-persisted when a run resumes.

findings.title: Change is several times over the stated budget, with extra mechanisms beyond the request
findings.detail: The request budgeted about 30 net source lines. The diff adds about 150 net source lines across 10 files: per-stream truncation flags in runProcess, JSON-escaped credential variants in redactCredentials, global HTTP redaction, redaction of prompt inputs, report redaction and the privacy-filter change. Some of this is defensible hardening, but it widens the review surface and touches systems the request declared out of scope.
findings.failure_scenario: Unrelated subsystems (MCP output, HTTP API, the process runner, credential matching) change behaviour in a PR scoped to gate-output redaction.

gold.summary: Redacting the carry early emits suffixes of overlapping registered credentials.
ANSI stripping after framing and tail cuts leaves accidental credential fragments visible.

findings.title: Defer overlapping credential replacement until the match is complete
findings.detail: Redacting the pending buffer immediately can replace a shorter registered credential before a longer credential finishes arriving. Retaining overlap after that replacement cannot recover the longer match, so its remaining secret text reaches gate results and downstream storage and feedback. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/gate-redaction-review.test.ts". The overlapping-credentials test failed with Expected: "[redacted]", Received: "[redacted]-secret-suffix".
findings.failure_scenario: Register both "synthetic-prefix" and "synthetic-prefix-secret-suffix", then emit the longer credential in two stdout chunks: "synthetic-prefix" and "-secret-suffix". runGates returns "[redacted]-secret-suffix".

findings.title: Normalize terminal formatting before the runner truncates output
findings.detail: Runner redaction does not remove terminal formatting, while redactGateStreams normalizes only after the runner's 64k tail cut. A formatted credential crossing that cut loses its prefix before normalization, leaving a fragment that subsequent redaction cannot recognize. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/gate-redaction-review.test.ts". The normalization test failed with Expected: "[redacted]xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx", Received: "kk-credential-footerxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx".
findings.failure_scenario: Register "synthetic-colored-" + "k" repeated 65,000 times + "-credential-footer". Insert an ANSI color sequence after character 12 and append 5,980 filler characters. runGates stores the credential suffix "kk-credential-footer" in its final output.

gold.summary: Configuration errors and encoded feed diagnostics can disclose registered secrets.
A failure after configuration replacement leaves initialization partially applied.
Doctor omits health probes for implicit providers and presets lacking an explicit health URL.
The command fake permits mutating operations during read-only diagnosis.
The registration test does not exercise preservation of existing vendor settings.

findings.title: Apply changed config to an already-running daemon
findings.detail: The service step only checks the preflight daemon status. If init writes new providers or a merge policy while the daemon is healthy, it skips installation/restart. Factory loads these settings at startup, so setup reports success while the daemon retains its old configuration. Command `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review.ts" reload` printed providers.added=[claude,codex,local-1234], effects=[smoke,mcp], then failed: `AssertionError: new provider config must reach the already-running daemon`.
findings.failure_scenario: A healthy daemon is running when init detects a new local provider or adds github.merge="pr". Config is written, but subsequent runs still use the previous catalog or merge default.

findings.title: Check requested repository access before writing config
findings.detail: Doctor runs before repositories supplied through --repo or prompts are considered, and only reads a repository already in config. Fresh setup therefore never verifies access or organization SSO for its requested repository. Command `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review.ts" repo`, with a fake repository API returning an SSO 403, printed `{"code":0,"ghReads":[],"effects":["smoke","mcp"]}` and failed: `AssertionError: init must reject a requested repository with denied SSO access`.
findings.failure_scenario: On an empty config, run init --yes --repo private-org/denied with gh authenticated but lacking organization SSO authorization. Setup writes config and proceeds without detecting the access failure.

findings.title: Run smoke checks against the effective provider catalog
findings.detail: The production smoke adapter calls the existing smoke main, which uses hard-coded PROVIDERS/MODELS rather than the config catalog. Newly detected local providers and custom endpoints are never exercised; both native CLIs are always exercised even when doctor permits one to be missing. Command `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review.ts" smoke` enumerated checks with a zero budget and no network. It reported detected=[claude,codex,local-1234], but smoke names contained only built-in providers, then failed: `AssertionError: smoke must exercise the detected local provider`.
findings.failure_scenario: Init detects a server on port 1234 and saves local-1234, but smoke never invokes it. Alternatively, a machine with only Claude passes preflight with a Codex warning and then fails smoke by invoking the absent Codex CLI.

gold.summary: Nesting Seatbelt around internally sandboxed CLIs prevents tool-enabled invocations from starting.
Scanning ordinary agent output for sandbox diagnostics can discard successful invocations.
Ordinary gate output mentioning sandbox failures can turn a successful check into a confinement error.
The live confinement smoke accepts refusal even when enforcement should work.

findings.title: Allow Codex to initialize without writing its shared state directory
findings.detail: The new outer profile denies writes outside the checkout and scratch, but Codex still inherits its normal CODEX_HOME and ordinary tool-enabled calls do not receive --ephemeral. Codex initializes its session rollout under CODEX_HOME/sessions before executing the agent; denying that write prevents normal invocations from starting. The substitute CLI tests never exercise this initialization.
findings.failure_scenario: On a host where the signal and nested-sandbox probes succeed, start a default tool-enabled Codex invocation with CODEX_HOME outside the checkout and scratch. Its rollout initialization encounters a denied write and the invocation fails before doing useful work.

findings.title: Detect executable command substitutions inside shell arguments
findings.failure_scenario: Either harness emits a shell tool call containing echo "$(pkill -f marker)". The shell executes pkill, but signalWarnings emits no warning.

gold.summary: A bare executable magic match rejects valid image bytes with an incidental signature.

findings.title: Restore all requested inert media exemptions
findings.detail: INERT_MEDIA_PATH includes only five image formats. Fonts, audio, video, PDFs, several images, and 3D models explicitly required by the request now block. Running `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-MnwSDK/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-MnwSDK/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-MnwSDK/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-MnwSDK/claude-501/review-repro.ts` against the committed media fixtures produced binary-content/block findings for asset.pdf, asset.wav, and asset.woff2. The new tests explicitly expect this contradictory behavior.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a normal binary WOFF2 font or PDF without Allow: binary; the audit blocks publication instead of passing.

findings.title: Do not classify visible executable text as binary
findings.detail: modeRequiresAllowance applies to every executable file, regardless of content. Consequently, ordinary shell scripts now require Allow: binary even though their complete content is reviewable. The reproduction command above committed run.sh containing `#!/bin/sh\necho hello\n` with mode 100755 and returned a binary-content/block finding for run.sh.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a tracked executable text script without Allow: binary; the audit incorrectly blocks the change.

findings.title: Do not treat arbitrary text substrings as binary formats
findings.detail: isForbiddenFormat searches entire blobs for signatures including the ordinary strings `MZ` and `ustar`. textAt then removes matching files from the text classification. The reproduction command above added example.ts containing only `export const archiveFormat = "ustar";` and returned a binary-content/block finding for example.ts. Fully visible source and documentation can therefore require binary allowances.
findings.failure_scenario: A TypeScript file mentions ustar, or documentation includes MZ, and the audit blocks it as hidden binary content despite a complete textual diff.

gold.summary: Detached descendants survive invocation cleanup and keep modifying the worktree.
Process cleanup returns while owned descendants are still alive.
Discarding changes replaces the cleanup error that should trigger round recovery.

findings.title: Finally cleanup can bypass round-failure recovery
findings.detail:
After checkoutCommitted exhausts its retry and throws WorktreeCleanError, the gates finally block still calls discardChanges. If an untracked file remains and that cleanup also fails, its ordinary CommandError replaces WorktreeCleanError. This catch then rethrows, failing the run. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-377-probes.ts"`. Output: `cleanup error: CommandError
round recovery recognizes error: false
Command failed (1): git clean -fdq
warning: could not remove untracked`.
findings.failure_scenario: A failed implement round leaves an untracked directory that both clean attempts cannot remove; discardChanges encounters the same directory and fails, causing a run failure instead of the next round.

findings.title: Process-group killing still leaves detached descendants alive
findings.detail: The new cleanup only signals and polls the original process group. A descendant started with detached:true has its own group and survives invocation completion. This leaves the central whole-process-tree requirement unresolved. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-377-probes.ts"`. Output: `invocation exit: 0\nbackground descendant alive after invocation: true\nbackground writer still writing: true`.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer's test runner spawns a detached writer with ignored stdio, then exits or is stopped. runProcess returns while the writer continues modifying the worktree during cleanup.

gold.summary: Run-wide scratch roots let one invocation cleanup kill another invocation writer.
A recycled leader PID claims unrelated processes through reused group or session identifiers.

findings.title: Do not claim unrelated orphan processes based on their cwd
findings.detail: Birth time, orphan status, and a shared directory do not prove invocation ownership. This heuristic adds unrelated processes to the set that receives SIGTERM/SIGKILL. I reproduced this with an independently launched, unmarked /bin/sleep orphan in the invocation's cwd: completing runProcess returned {"exitCode":0,"unrelatedOrphanAlive":false}. A focused assertion also fails. Command: bun -e 'import {hiddenDarwinProcessMember as member} from "./src/util/processes-darwin.ts"; import {strictEqual} from "node:assert"; strictEqual(member(42,new Map([[42,1]]),new Set(),100,[process.cwd()],()=>101,()=>({path:process.cwd()})),false,"an unrelated orphan must not belong to this invocation");'. Output:
findings.failure_scenario: While an invocation runs, a separate launcher starts a background platform process in the same worktree or scratch directory and exits. On macOS, if its environment is hidden, cleanup classifies this unrelated orphan as invocation-owned and kills it.

gold.summary: Pre-aborted shutdown with failed leader inspection references timer cleanup before initialization and never settles.

findings.title: Do not infer process ownership from an orphan's working directory
findings.detail:
An unrelated orphan born during an invocation is classified as its descendant when it shares the working directory. Shutdown consequently signals processes belonging to other invocations or the user. Reproduced with this exact command:
bun -e 'import {runProcess} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; import {spawnSync} from "node:child_process"; let sibling; try { const r=await runProcess({cmd:[process.execPath,"-e","console.log(\"ready\"); setTimeout(()=>{},300)"],cwd:process.cwd(),env:process.env,onStdoutLine:()=>{const s=spawnSync(process.execPath,["-e","const c=require(\"node:child_process\").spawn(\"/bin/sleep\",[\"30\"],{env:{},detached:true,stdio:\"ignore\"}); console.log(c.pid); c.unref()"],{en
findings.failure_scenario: While an invocation runs, an independent launcher starts a detached process with an empty environment in the same checkout and exits. Finishing the invocation kills that unrelated process.

findings.title: Actual descendants can still outlive successful invocation shutdown
findings.detail:
The acknowledged fallback limitation leaves the requested whole-tree shutdown incomplete: a detached descendant with a replaced environment and a different cwd survives, while runProcess returns success and permits cleanup. Reproduced with this exact command:
bun -e 'import {runProcess} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; let pid; try {const r=await runProcess({cmd:[process.execPath,"-e","const c=require(\"node:child_process\").spawn(\"/bin/sleep\",[\"30\"],{cwd:\"/\",env:{},detached:true,stdio:\"ignore\"}); console.log(c.pid); c.unref()"],cwd:process.cwd(),env:process.env}); pid=Number(r.stdout.trim()); let alive=true; try{process.kill(pid,0)}catch{alive=false} console.log("invocation exit:",r.exitC
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer launches a detached writer with env:{} and cwd outside the checkout, writing into the checkout through an absolute path. The implementer exits; shutdown reports success while the writer continues racing cleanup.

gold.summary: A single extracted test command is treated as proof of a multi-step criterion.

findings.title: Do not substitute an entire criterion from one embedded test command
findings.detail: The matcher extracts a Bun command from arbitrary instructions and ignores additional verification steps. A passing unit test therefore turns a blocked application HTTP check into met, allowing normalizeVerify to approve unverified behavior. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {applyGateEvidence as apply} from "./src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts"; const sha="a".repeat(40), result={command:"bun test",ok:true,exitCode:0,output:"a.test.ts:\n(pass) unit"}; const v=apply({criteria:[{id:"A",status:"blocked"}]},{acceptance_criteria:[{id:"A",how_to_verify:"Run `bun test a.test.ts` then start the app and check HTTP 200"}]},{scenarios:[]},sha,{sha,checks:[{verdict:"pass",result,testCommand:"bun test"}]}
findings.failure_scenario: A criterion requires running a unit test and starting the application to check HTTP behavior. Gates pass the unit test, but the verifier cannot start the application because loopback listening is denied. The factory incorrectly marks the entire criterion met.

gold.summary: Free-text claim detection still lets model wording steer gate-evidence substitution.

findings.title: Unrelated skipped tests disable all gate-evidence substitution
findings.detail: A skipped test anywhere invalidates the entire gate run, even when the requested file passed completely. This repository intentionally skips real Seatbelt tests inside confined gates, so its normal successful suite cannot unblock loopback verification. An isolated `bun run -` check using passedFiles=['test/loopback.test.ts'] printed `clean suite: met`; adding skippedFiles=['test/sandbox.test.ts'] printed `unrelated skipped Seatbelt tests: blocked`.
findings.failure_scenario: The confined full-suite gate passes the loopback test and skips nested Seatbelt tests. The reader cannot bind loopback, and verification still ends as environment-blocked despite successful coverage of the requested test.

findings.title: Ordinary mentions of gates invalidate independent verification
findings.detail: The sanitizer treats any standalone 'gate' mention as a factory citation, and checks global notes for every criterion. Consequently, notes such as 'Independently tested gate timeout handling.' downgrade every met criterion to blocked, including rows containing independently observed passing commands. The isolated `bun run -` check returned status `blocked` while retaining evidence `bun test test/loopback.test.ts: 1 pass, 0 fail`.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier successfully tests gate-related functionality and mentions that functionality in its notes. Criteria requiring inspection or commands unavailable in gate records become blocked and can terminate the run as needs_human.

gold.summary: An inherited Git configuration selector redirects trusted SSH lookup into the checkout.
Trusted remote-dependent credential and SSH settings no longer apply during push.
Manual landing publishes a fork branch to the upstream repository.
Forcing HTTPS during manual push bypasses working SSH authentication.

findings.title: Preserve trusted helpers selected by remote-URL conditions
findings.detail: Replacing the common config removes remote URLs needed by trusted global includeIf.hasconfig:remote.*.url conditions. A network-free probe with a global conditional credential.helper returned credentials before isolation, but invoking the same credential lookup through the wrapper produced "fatal: could not read Username for 'https://example.invalid': terminal prompts disabled" and exit 128. Thus existing global authentication settings can stop working on every push path.
findings.failure_scenario: The global config conditionally includes a credential helper for repositories whose remote URL matches https://example.invalid/**. The checkout matches, but the isolated push config contains no remote URL, so authentication fails.

findings.title: Preserve the trusted transport for SSH-authenticated installations
findings.detail: The manual land push now always uses HTTPS. An installation that previously pushed through an SSH origin using SSH keys or a global core.sshCommand now needs separate HTTPS credentials. Preserving core.sshCommand in the wrapper does not help because HTTPS never invokes SSH. This violates the requirement to retain existing SSH authentication.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner uses git@github.com:MattFlower/limitless.git with working SSH authentication and has no HTTPS credential helper or global URL rewrite. The previously successful manual land push now fails authentication.

gold.summary: Manual push reloads mutable clone configuration after its final validation snapshot.
Inherited Git configuration causes validation and push to inspect different settings.
An exact upstream URL requirement rejects supported forks and alternate origin spellings.

findings.title: Apply config isolation to delivery and land-queue pushes
findings.detail: Neither pushBranch nor pushExistingBranch was changed. Both still consume repository-scoped URL rewrites and command settings through worktreeGit. A local probe using repository-scoped url.<ext-command>.pushInsteadOf and protocol.ext.allow=always executed a marker-writing command in both paths. Command: bun run "$TMPDIR/review-push-config.ts". Output: "delivery: marker=true, exactSHA=true" and "land: marker=true, exactSHA=true". These are unresolved security requirements of this change.
findings.failure_scenario: PR code plants a repository-scoped pushInsteadOf rewrite to an ext transport. Delivery or the land queue pushes the pinned SHA and executes the planted command.

findings.title: Exclude repository config instead of checking it before use
findings.detail: The final snapshot does not isolate the subsequent push: safe_git still reads live repository config and pushes to origin. A child left running by unconfined checks can modify config after the comparison. A probe using the exact added functions, then planting remote.origin.receivepack between the final comparison and push, executed the command. Command: bash "$TMPDIR/review-manual-config.sh". Output: "manual: marker=true after final validation" and "manual: exactSHA=true".
findings.failure_scenario: A PR-spawned background process installs receivepack after config_after is read but before git push reads the config.

findings.title: Allow harmless local configuration without blocking landing
findings.detail: The allowlist rejects every unlisted local key before installation or checks, including ordinary user.name, user.email, core.autocrlf, and additional remotes. The request requires ignoring repository config for pushes, rather than making such repositories impossible to land. The local probe command bash "$TMPDIR/review-manual-config.sh" produced "Repository git config key user.name is not allowed; refusing to land" and "local identity rejected".
findings.failure_scenario: An owner sets git config user.name in a normal checkout and runs land-pr.sh; the script now exits before running checks.

gold.summary: Unresolved tool calls accumulate without a bound during a live invocation.

findings.title: Unresolved calls can be evicted without ever counting
findings.detail: Calls awaiting results remain uncounted until finish(), but eviction permanently discards them first. Consequently, six identical calls with missing results can escape detection entirely, violating the requirement that missing results retain today's counting. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const detector = new LoopDetector(100); for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) detector.observe("shell", "poll", `missing-${i}`); for (let i = 0; i < 12; i++) detector.observe("Read", { path: `file-${i}` }); const result = detector.finish(); console.log("finish:", result); assert.equal(result, "repeated the same shel
findings.failure_scenario: An invocation emits six identical shell calls whose results never arrive, then twelve distinct calls. No observation reports a loop, and finish() returns null, allowing the invocation to succeed despite the repeated unresolved calls.

gold.summary: A completed parallel call is classified as repetitive before unresolved predecessors establish progress.

findings.title: Preserve the previous result hash after window eviction
findings.detail: Deleting the result baseline makes a changed result count as repetition when its preceding call has left the window. Reproduction: `bun -e 'import {LoopDetector as D} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new D(100); d.observe("shell","poll","a"); d.observeResult("a","old"); for(let i=0;i<12;i++) d.observe("Read",i); for(let i=0;i<6;i++){d.observe("shell","poll",String(i)); d.observeResult(String(i),"new");} console.log(d.finish());'` outputs `repeated the same shell call 6 times`; expected `null`, because the first new result is progress and only five subsequent calls repeat it.
findings.failure_scenario: A poll returns 'old', twelve unrelated calls evict its entry, then six polls return 'new'. The detector stops the agent one repetition too early.

gold.summary: A historical policy edit keeps invalidating implementer selections made after that edit.

findings.title: Preserve stickiness for implementers selected after an edit
findings.detail: changedCells is never cleared, so every subsequent round suppresses preferred implementers outside an edited cell—even implementers selected after the edit through normal escalation. This sends a run back to a weaker model instead of retaining its escalated implementer. Reproduction command: `bun "$TMPDIR/routing-sticky-review.ts"`. Output: `{"escalated":"claude/opus","next":"codex/luna@medium"}`, followed by `AssertionError: An implementer selected after the edit should remain sticky` (expected `claude/opus`, actual `codex/luna@medium`).
findings.failure_scenario: Set implement.small to ["codex/luna"], escalate with minTier: 5 to claude/opus, then route the next round with prefer set to that Opus selection and no further policy edit. The router returns codex/luna@medium.

gold.summary: A pinned candidate slot deadline exits without recording the chain-exhaustion question.

findings.title: Keep previously exhausted implementers excluded after escalation
findings.detail: The tried-implementer exclusion applies only on the escalation round. Subsequent rounds pass only a preference for the current implementer, allowing routing back to an earlier exhausted candidate if the current one becomes unavailable. Probe: `bun test "$TMPDIR/chain-probe.test.ts" -t 'probe escalated chain'`, using a temporary copy of the pipeline fixture with chain [alpha/m, beta/m], failing gates, and beta disabled after its first invocation. Output: `PROBE needs_human ["alpha/m","alpha/m","beta/m","alpha/m"]`; the assertion expecting ["alpha/m","alpha/m","beta/m"] failed. This spends another implementation round on an exhausted model instead of stopping for human intervention.
findings.failure_scenario: A consumes its two implementation rounds, escalation selects B, and B becomes disabled before the next round. The router invokes A again despite A having already exhausted its rounds.

gold.summary: A fixed review-time cutoff excludes worktrees created before the sidecar-writing release actually started.

findings.title: Determine legacy eligibility from installation history, not commit time
findings.detail: The fixed cutoff excludes worktrees created by an older release after #323 was authored but before that installation upgraded. Those runs retain null provenance, so resume skips registration and fails with "Missing trusted Git paths". Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {Database} from "bun:sqlite"; import {strict as assert} from "node:assert"; const db=new Database(":memory:"); db.exec(`CREATE TABLE runs(id); INSERT INTO runs VALUES(1); CREATE TABLE stages(run_id,name,started_at,finished_at,status); INSERT INTO stages VALUES(1,"prepare",1791185704000,1791185705000,"succeeded"); CREATE TABLE events(run_id,type,ts);`); db.exec(await Bun.file("src/db/migrations/20261005T134145-worktree-proven
findings.failure_scenario: An installation continues running the pre-#323 release until October 6. It creates and parks a run on October 5, then upgrades. Despite having a valid legacy worktree, that run is excluded by the migration and fails on resume.

gold.summary: A definitively refused CI rerun remains pending indefinitely.
Passing security-test output incorrectly prevents a transient CI rerun.

findings.title: Explicitly rejected reruns remain pending forever
findings.detail: The rerun is claimed before the POST, but a definitive rejection such as HTTP 422 leaves its outcome as rerun_requested. Subsequent inspections wait for a newer workflow attempt that will never exist and suppress ci.needs_fix. Temporary regression command: bun test "$TMPDIR/limitless-ci-adversarial.test.ts". Output: "rejected rerun state rerun_requested needs_fix 0" and "Expected length: 1 / Received length: 0".
findings.failure_scenario: A timed-out job qualifies for rerun, but GitHub rejects POST actions/jobs/21/rerun with HTTP 422. No new attempt starts, and every subsequent poll leaves the failure pending without ci.needs_fix.

findings.title: One CI inspection error starves later PR observations
findings.detail: classifyCi throws on incomplete REST evidence, and the exception escapes record and aborts the repository's entire observation loop. A persistent error on the first PR therefore prevents later PR snapshots and merge/close transitions from being processed. Temporary regression command: bun test "$TMPDIR/limitless-ci-adversarial.test.ts". Output: "second PR snapshot null" followed by "expect(received).not.toBeNull() / Received: null".
findings.failure_scenario: Two factory PRs are tracked in one repository. The first PR's job logs consistently return HTTP 404, such as after log expiration. Every poll aborts before saving the second PR's observation.

findings.title: Pre-existing restart-repair readiness assertion fails
findings.detail: bun test test/pipeline.test.ts --test-name-pattern 'verify-change: restart-repair' fails on both HEAD and the base commit with "expect(received).toBeDefined() / Received: undefined". The fixed readiness wait expires before the fixture reaches its repair-review checkpoint. This failure predates the change.
findings.failure_scenario: Run the restart-repair test in this environment; resume remains undefined after the 300 iterations of the 20 ms wait.

gold.summary: Rate-limit refusals leave rerun claims unresolved across cooldowns and restarts.
ANSI-colored Bun failures and pytest security failures are missed by the retry exclusion.

findings.title: Isolate CI inspection failures from other PR observations
findings.detail: A classifier exception escapes record() and aborts the repository's remaining PR observations. Because ciPending persists, a permanently unavailable log repeats this starvation every poll. As written, an experiment that pins triage to a decision-capable model fails whenever the model is unsure, even though its answer is usable.
findings.failure_scenario: models {triage: ["<decision model>"]}. The model declines with lastResort=true, the next route finds no untried candidates, and the run goes to needs_human instead of using its answer.

findings.title: Chain mode ignores independence even as a tie-break between `|` alternatives
findings.detail: With `c.chain` set, every candidate gets rank 0, so `a|b` alternatives are ordered only by provider preference and headroom. If a review chain is `claude/opus|codex/sol` and the implementer is openai, codex/sol can win on headroom and trigger the 'because this run pinned it' warning, even though the operator offered an independent alternative in the same group. The request says the chain wins over soft rules, not that soft rules stop breaking ties among alternatives the operator called interchangeable. The existing post-review log "Review done by the implementer's vendor (no other vendor available)" is also untrue in this case.
findings.failure_scenario: Implementer is codex/sol (openai) and models.review = ["claude/opus|codex/sol"], with codex having more headroom. Review runs on codex/sol, logs the pinned-vendor warning and also logs 'no other vendor available'.

gold.summary: Arbitrary assertion text mentioning a timeout is classified as a transient CI failure.
Retry eligibility ignores security failures outside the selected error line.

An accepted rerun with a lost response is never reconciled to its later result.

findings.title: A classifyCi exception aborts observation of every later PR in the repository, indefinitely
findings.detail: record() awaits classifyCi with no error handling. classifyCi throws in many places (Incomplete failing check, Incomplete CI log, Ambiguous originating CI job, Outdated CI check completion, any non-200 REST read). The throw propagates out of observe(), whose loop `for (const [i, pr] of known.entries()) await record(...)` stops, so PRs after the failing one are never recorded. ciPending was already saved as true, so the same PR throws again every cycle. Merges, closes, review and comment items for the other PRs are lost, setGithubAccess(repo, null) never runs, and delivered runs waiting on a merge stay stuck. Before this change, record() could not fail on REST data.
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced in a copy of the repo with dependencies installed. PR 1 has rollup FAILURE but the REST check-run for 'test' shows success, and PR 2 is set to MERGED. After 10 poll cycles, PR 2's saved data is still undefined, and the logs repeat 'GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete failing chec

findings.title: The failure signature uses the first line containing 'fail' or 'error', often an echoed action input
findings.detail: ciSignature uses `lines.find(l => /timed out after|##\[error\]|\b(?:error|fail(?:ed|ure)?)\b/i.test(l))`. GitHub Actions logs print each step's inputs (for example `fail-on-cache-miss: false` for actions/cache) long before the real failure. That line becomes the signature 'line' for every failure of the check. Ledger rows then record a meaningless 'failing test or error line'. Different failures at the same SHA share a signature, which breaks the 'one rerun per PR, SHA and signature' identity, and flakes cannot be told apart by test.
findings.failure_scenario: In my scratch test, ciSignature('test', log, 'failure') returned 'fail-on-cache-miss: false' for a log whose real failure lines were '##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.' and 'AssertionError: expected 1 to be 2'.

findings.title: A rerun is requested while the workflow run is still in progress, which uses up the only rerun and can raise an access problem
findings.detail: Classification starts as soon as the rollup turns FAILURE, which happens while sibling jobs are still running. The code claims the rerun (claimCiRerun) and POSTs actions/jobs/{id}/rerun without checking that the run is completed. GitHub refuses to rerun jobs of a run that is still in progress (403). The claim is already spent, so the next pass sees the prior row as rerun_requested and emits ci.needs_fix, and the transient failure never gets its rerun. The 403 also goes through call() and ciCall, which treat it as an access problem: the repository is blocked with backoff and a 'forbidden' github.access_problem item is emitted.
findings.failure_scenario: In a workflow with jobs 'smoke' and 'test', 'smoke' times out at minute 5 while 'test' runs until minute 15. The poller sees FAILURE and POSTs the rerun for 'smoke', and GitHub returns 403 because the run is in progress. The row stays rerun_requested, and the next poll emits ci.needs_fix without a r

findings.title: Fail-fast matrix cancellations count as transient, so a pass on rerun is logged as false flake evidence
findings.detail: Any 'cancelled' conclusion at the current head counts as transient. In a matrix with fail-fast (the default), one leg failing cancels the others. Each cancelled leg is rerun, usually passes, and gets outcome failed_then_passed. The request says a rerun that passes at the same SHA is the only evidence of nondeterminism that counts, so the ledger records nondeterminism that never happened. It also spends paid CI on reruns that were never needed.
findings.failure_scenario: In a matrix test with legs [ubuntu, macos] and fail-fast: true, the ubuntu leg fails an assertion and the macos leg is cancelled. The macos leg is rerun, passes, and the ledger row shows outcome 'failed_then_passed' for macos.

findings.title: The main-red state resets while main's newest commit is still running checks, which creates duplicate ci.main_red items
findings.detail: A check counts as red only if the latest run on main's current HEAD is completed with a failure. When another commit lands on main while the check is still broken, its runs are in_progress, so red becomes false. Per-PR suppression lifts during that window, so the PR can be rerun or get ci.needs_fix. When main finishes red again, `episode` goes up and a new ci.main_red item is emitted. The request asks for one ci.main_red item per repository while main is red.
findings.failure_scenario: Main is red on 'test' (episode 1). A PR lands on main, and while the new HEAD's 'test' is in progress a factory PR fails 'test' and gets rerun or reported as needs_fix. Main finishes red, and a second ci.main_red item (episode 2) is emitted.

findings.title: The feed excerpt is the first 2000 characters of the job log, not the failure
findings.detail: emit() stores `quote(excerpt.trim().slice(0, 2000))`, where excerpt is the full job log. Actions logs start with runner, image and checkout setup output, so the excerpt rarely includes the failing test or error. That makes ci.needs_fix much less useful to whoever reads the feed.
findings.failure_scenario: For a typical 50 KB Actions log the ci.needs_fix excerpt contains only 'Current runner version', 'Operating System', 'Runner Image' and checkout lines.

findings.title: Observations the head epoch refuses are now dropped entirely, an unrequested behavior change
findings.detail: Previously record() ignored observePrHead's result and still saved the snapshot (state, merge, feed items); only the head write was refused. Now a refusal returns early. While a round's push mark exists (including one left by a crashed run until it becomes terminal), the PR's merges, closes and comments are not observed.
findings.failure_scenario: A round run crashes between beginPrPush and endPrPush and stays non-terminal. The PR is merged meanwhile, but the poller does not record the merge until the run is marked terminal.

findings.title: A second migration adds a column to a table this same change creates
findings.detail: Neither migration has shipped, so `rerun_job` belongs in the CREATE TABLE in 20261005T0737-ci-failures.sql. A separate ALTER adds churn.

The next restart then fails. The operator can't fix it with `limitless catalog remove`, because that needs the running daemon's API. The only ways out are editing SQLite by hand or reverting config. findings.detail: `remove()` refuses only when `store.routingCells()` names the model. The effective policy also has an eval overlay layer (policy.json, read by `readPolicy` at boot and validated against `this.models`). If that overlay names a runtime model, for example one written by `eval policy --write` after evaluating it, DELETE succeeds. The next Factory construction then throws `Invalid routing policy …`. findings.detail: To read runtime models, `main()` now opens `new Store(cfg.paths.db)`, which runs migrations on the live database from the smoke process. It also filters every provider check by `getProviderEnabledOverride`, and replaces the 'missing provider' throws with `continue` or `return checks`.
